actions.name: used Telegram as a command-and-control (C2) infrastructure to push malware
actions.description: MOIS cyber actors are responsible for using Telegram as a command-and-control (C2) infrastructure to push malware targeting Iranian dissidents, journalists opposed to Iran, and other opposition groups around the world.

actions.name: deployed multiple versions of malware to infect Windows machines

actions.name: used social engineering to deliver stage 1 masquerading malware
actions.description: Threat actors relied upon social engineering to deliver malware and infect victim devices by masquerading as a known individual or technical support from the social messaging platform and convincing the victim to accept a file transfer consisting of the masquerading stage 1 malware.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: infected victim device and launched persistent implant stage 2 malware

actions.name: configured Telegram bot as command and control (C2) for persistent implant malware
actions.description: At stage 2, the Iran MOIS cyber actors configured a command and control (C2) using a Telegram bot, allowing bidirectional communication between the compromised device and api.telegram[.]org.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: performed defensive evasion and persistence via Windows registry autorun
actions.description: Malware performed defensive evasion, excluded directories, allowed PowerShell to execute malware without warning, and added a reference to malware in the Windows registry to autorun stage 2 malware, which served as persistent implants.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: exfiltrated data using multiple malware samples
actions.description: The malware campaign used multiple malware samples including MicDriver.exe/dll, Winappx.exe, MsCache.exe, RuntimeSSH.exe, and smqdservice.exe to exfiltrate data such as screen recordings, audio, cache captures, compressed files, and staged compressed files to api.telegram[.]org.
